props.title: Schizopolis

sections.content: Steven Soderbergh's mind-bending **Schizopolis** (1997) represents his most experimental and meta-textual work, arriving between his indie breakthrough **sex, lies and videotape** (1989) and mainstream success with **Out of Sight** (1998). Soderbergh himself plays multiple roles, including a corporate speechwriter and his doppelganger, in this absurdist comedy that deliberately fractures narrative conventions. The film shares DNA with the fourth-wall-breaking techniques of **Adaptation** (2002) and the identity-swapping complexity of **Mulholland Drive** (2001), while predating both.

sections.content: The film's innovative approach to language - with characters speaking in corporate jargon, literal descriptions of actions, and complete nonsense - influenced later experimental works like **Sorry to Bother You** (2018) and **I'm Thinking of Ending Things** (2020). Soderbergh's guerrilla filmmaking approach, shooting on minimal budget with friends and family, established a template he would return to with projects like **High Flying Bird** (2019) and **Unsane** (2018), both shot on iPhones. SUBHEAD: Meta-Cinema and Corporate Satire

**Schizopolis** mercilessly satirizes corporate culture, self-help movements, and the film industry itself. Its structure, divided into three segments showing overlapping events from different perspectives, predates similar narrative experiments in **Time Code** (2000) and **The Rules of Attraction** (2002). The film's treatment of identity and reality distortion shares thematic concerns with **Being John Malkovich** (1999) and **Persona** (1966), while its corporate satire anticipates **Office Space** (1999) and **Sorry to Bother You** (2018).
